The Sea

The sea does not argue,
it only arrives—
a long grey argument
that never learns its point.

By morning it has left
a hundred small agreements
on the shore: shells, salt,
a bottle wearing its name.

Children wade in the shallows,
teaching the water
how to be looked at.

At night the moon pulls up
the same old rope,
and the sea, patient,
lets itself be tied.

The Sea

The sea does not hurry,
yet it is always gone —
the tide takes back its promises
and the gulls take back the sound.

Between the waves, some patience:
salt learning how to be a stone,
foam stitching white seams
through a hem of blue.

Look long enough and it stops
being water, starts being weather,
a slow weather
with a long memory.

And still, at night, it comes —
not asking to be saved,
just

0/2:
The Sea

The sea does not ask,
it only answers—
a long grey hush
between one wave and the next.

Salt in the wind,
a gull's small punctuation,
the horizon
keeping its own counsel.

Come as you are,
with your weathered names
and your leaking hulls—
the water will hold
what the shore forgets.

And when the moon pulls,
and the tide turns its slow page,
we will have been
somewhere the deep remembers.
